summary: A failing property exposed a console lock-order inversion between FsCheck QuickThrowOnFailure output and Expecto console redirection. The property helpers use an IRunner whose fixture, argument and shrink callbacks do no output; OnFinished returns for Passed and throws FsCheck Runner.onFinishedToString for every other result, retaining counterexamples and replay information. Keep both property helpers on this runner. CI adds eight impossible properties to the complete parallel suite and bounds execution to 120 seconds plus a 10-second kill grace. Its checker rejects timeout/kill, exit zero and any summary without exactly eight failed plus errored tests. This guards the failure path as well as the ordinary green run; a green-only test cannot detect this lock inversion. Lockstep is a standalone fixture/stack console and bench uses BenchmarkDotNet, so neither shares the affected runner. Source configuration and historical diagnosis do not establish current hosted CI or native acceptance; refresh those separately.
title: Keep FsCheck callbacks silent inside parallel Expecto tests
